messages:
alex: Heads-up: new billing/quotas changes launching Wed 2026-05-14. This touches free-tier runaways, first-time overage forgiveness, and how unused promo credits are handled. Short summary below.

maria: quick TL;DR?

alex: 1) Transient Overage Forgiveness (TOF): the first single overage event per account in a 90-day window will be automatically covered by a small forgiveness buffer (up to $50 equivalent).

alex: 2) Per-project burst tokens: free-tier projects get a small monthly pool of burst tokens (tokens/month) that allow short spikes without immediate throttling.

alex: 3) Promo rollover -> buffer: unused Redwood-issued promo credits will roll into a new "grace buffer" account-level credit at month-end. These buffer credits can be auto-applied to TOF events or short SRC bursts.

sanjay: How do burst tokens differ from the SRC concept we discussed before?

linda: Burst tokens are a monthly bucket for short spikes; SRC (sustained-rate cap) is a continuous soft throttling policy. Both can operate together: burst only protects short spikes below sustained limits.

maria: Will any of this show up on invoices?

alex: Invoice change: new line items will appear for "Grace buffer applied" when buffer credits were used, and "TOF adjustment" if TOF covered an overage. No pricing change to unit rates. Full audit trail will still be in Billing > Usage.

billing-bot: Note: rollout window 2026-05-14 02:00 UTC -> 2026-05-14 06:00 UTC. Feature flags: tof-enabled, burst-buckets, promo-rollover. See deploy: /deploys/1960-TOF-rollout.

sanjay: Which accounts are eligible for TOF and the buffer? startups? enterprise?

alex: Eligibility: TOF & buffer apply to hosted pay-as-you-go and free-tier accounts only. Accounts with active enterprise contracts, Dedicated, or Private deployments are excluded. Partner-issued credits don't rollover.

linda: Support playbook (draft): 1) Confirm overage event in Console 2) Verify whether TOF auto-covered it (audit flag) 3) If TOF used and customer requests reversal, escalate to Billing for manual review 4) If buffer depleted, offer 1h trial uplift or recommend moving to Dedicated.

maria: Can customers opt-out of promo rollover?

alex: Yes — customers can opt-out in Billing Settings. Opt-out means unused promo credits expire normally instead of moving to the buffer. We'll add an opt-out toggle before rollout.

sanjay: Implementation detail for ops: how do we surface burst token consumption?

ops-bot: Dashboard update: new widgets - Burst tokens remaining per project, TOF events (count + account list), Buffer application log. Pager if >150 TOF events in 5m.

maria: Messaging plan: 1) pre-rollout internal FAQ and playbook to GTM/support at 09:00 PT tomorrow 2) customer banner + email on rollout day 3) blog post with examples and migration tips next week.

alex: Risk notes: TOF may be abused; finance set a $50 cap and one-time per 90 days. We'll monitor abuse signals and reserve right to revoke for accounts misusing.

linda: Samples for support to run quickly: check TOF status via API: ```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/billing/tof_status?account_id=acct_456
```

maria: I'll push the support snippets, opt-out UI mock, and email templates to the comms repo after the 09:00 sync.

alex: Thanks team. If you see anything odd in staging, tag #release-war-room immediately. We'll review post-rollout metrics at +24h and +72h.
